chunks: From him, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurarah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who left behind a brother from his father and mother and a grandfather. He said: 'The property is shared between them. Even if there were two brothers or a hundred, the grandfather would be with them as one of them; the grandfather receives what one of the brothers would receive.'
He said: 'And if he left behind a sister, the grandfather gets two shares and the sister gets one share. And if there were two sisters, the grandfather gets half and the two sisters get half.'
And he said: 'If he left behind brothers and sisters from both father and mother, the grandfather is like one of the brothers; for the male is equal to the share of two females.'

key_terms.لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ: For the male is the share of two females

ai.seo_question: How is the grandfather's share calculated in inheritance when there are brothers or sisters present?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific inheritance share of the paternal grandfather (*al-Jadd*) when competing with full siblings, establishing him as a single unit sharing equally with brothers or receiving half when competing with sisters. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction where the grandfather is treated as a descendant (*'Asaba* or *Dhu Fard*) rather than a separate class, resolving conflicts between the Quranic verse and prophetic practice. This ruling is crucial for understanding the hierarchy of heirs in Shia fiqh, particularly regarding the exclusion of the grandfather by sons but not by brothers.
